rubric.why: A community consists of populations of different species.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it includes populations of different species.

rubric.why: The populations live and interact in the same area or habitat.
rubric.description: States that the populations live in the same area or habitat.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning a shared area or habitat.

modelAnswer: A community is made up of populations of different species that live and interact in the same area or habitat.

rubric.why: A theory explains aspects or phenomena of the natural world.
rubric.description: Identifies a theory as an explanation of a natural phenomenon or aspect of the natural world.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing a theory as an explanation.

rubric.why: Scientific theories are supported by evidence gathered through observation and experimentation.
rubric.description: States that the explanation is supported by evidence or repeated observations and experiments.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the evidence-based nature of a theory.

modelAnswer: A theory is a well-supported explanation of an aspect of the natural world.
It is based on evidence from repeated observations and experiments.

rubric.why: Analysis organizes, summarizes, or interprets collected data.
rubric.description: States that data analysis organizes, summarizes, or interprets data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing how data are processed.

rubric.why: Analysis helps researchers reach conclusions, test a hypothesis, or identify patterns.
rubric.description: States that analysis is used to reach conclusions, test a hypothesis, or identify trends.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid purpose of analysing data.

modelAnswer: Data analysis is necessary to organize and interpret the collected data.
It helps us draw conclusions, test a hypothesis, and identify patterns or trends.

items.followUp: What is the function of mitochondria?

rubric.why: Cell organelles are structures found inside cells.
rubric.description: Identifies organelles as structures within a cell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying them as cell structures.

rubric.why: Different organelles perform particular functions in the cell.
rubric.description: States that organelles perform specific functions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning their specific functions.

modelAnswer: Cell organelles are specialized structures within a cell.
Each organelle performs a specific function.

items.followUp: Write the classification of a domestic cat from kingdom to species.

rubric.why: These are the human kingdom, phylum, and class.
rubric.description: Gives the kingdom, phylum, and class of humans.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for Animalia, Chordata, and Mammalia.

rubric.why: These are the human order, family, genus, and species.
rubric.description: Gives the order, family, genus, and species of humans.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for Primates, Hominidae, Homo, and sapiens.

modelAnswer: Kingdom: Animalia
Phylum: Chordata
Class: Mammalia
Order: Primates
Family: Hominidae
Genus: Homo
Species: sapiens (Homo sapiens)

rubric.why: Taxonomy deals with naming and classifying organisms.
rubric.description: Defines taxonomy as the naming and classification of organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming and classification.

rubric.why: Systematics studies organismal diversity and relationships among organisms.
rubric.description: Defines systematics by reference to diversity and relationships among organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both diversity and relationships.

modelAnswer: Taxonomy is the science of naming and classifying organisms.
Systematics is the study of the diversity of organisms and their relationships.

items.followUp: Name the three stages of interphase.

rubric.why: The cell cycle is the sequence of events in a cell from its formation until it divides.
rubric.description: Defines the cell cycle as the sequence of events from cell formation to division.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition.

rubric.why: The main phases are interphase and the mitotic (M) phase; interphase includes G1, S, and G2.
rubric.description: Names the main phases of the cell cycle.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming interphase and mitotic phase, or the three interphase stages and mitosis.

modelAnswer: The cell cycle is the sequence of events in a cell from its formation until it divides.
Its main phases are interphase and the mitotic (M) phase.
Interphase consists of G1, S, and G2 phases.

items.followUp: What is the result of nondisjunction during meiosis?

rubric.why: Nondisjunction is the failure of chromosomes to separate properly during cell division.
rubric.description: States that chromosomes fail to separate.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the separation failure.

rubric.why: This can produce cells or gametes with an abnormal chromosome number.
rubric.description: States that nondisjunction results in an abnormal chromosome number.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid chromosomal consequence.

modelAnswer: Nondisjunction is the failure of homologous chromosomes or sister chromatids to separate during cell division.
It can produce gametes with an abnormal number of chromosomes.
